subject: Edge Halo capacity: tri-region GPU counts & SOW checklist
messages:
From: Seth Cole <seth.cole@edgehalo.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Tri-region capacity ask + SOW checklist

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the call this morning — we had a productive session with product and infra leads. As we move toward signature for EH-1523, procurement asked me to confirm the committed GPU footprint by region for the SOW. High level ask: a committed baseline for US, EU, and APAC (Singapore) + burst allowances and failover rules.

Can you send a concise table we can put into the SOW (numbers, sku/instance types, typical sustained TPS/token estimates, and fallback policy)? Also our legal/procurement want a short SOW checklist (billing cadence, data residency note, and break/failover procedures).

Preferably by EOD tomorrow — procurement is targeting a DocuSign send early next week.

Thanks,
Seth
Seth Cole
Head of Platform Engineering
Edge Halo

Attachments: none

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Seth Cole <seth.cole@edgehalo.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 11:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tri-region capacity ask + SOW checklist

Hey Seth — appreciate the clear ask. I attached a working capacity table (edgehalo_capacity_table_v1.xlsx) and a one-page SOW checklist draft. Quick summary in-line below so procurement has something to paste into their template:

- Committed baseline (sustained): US 48 A100s (8 nodes), EU 24 A100s (4 nodes), APAC 24 A100s (4 nodes)
- Burst pool (on-demand reserve): US +20 A100s, EU +10 A100s, APAC +8 A100s; burst billed at overage rates per SOW
- Failover policy: regional failover to nearest region within same continent (APAC -> US fallback for limited features; full failover to EU only by explicit opt-in)
- Sequence length and latency SLO assumptions documented in sheet (95th percentile latency target: 250ms token path for gen workloads)

SOW checklist highlights: billing cadence (monthly in arrears), data residency (customer data stored in-region; logs routed to customer project), audit logs & SOC2 evidence statement, escalation SLA and credit matrix.

I've kept one column for "deal-triggered ramp" where we tie additional committed nodes to monthly usage thresholds (helpful for reserved capacity cadence). Please confirm whether the APAC fallback to US is acceptable from a compliance standpoint or if Edge Halo insists on APAC-only failover.

I'll stand up a cleaned PDF (edgehalo_sow_draft_v1.pdf) once you confirm the numbers.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Strategic Sales — Dedicated Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: edgehalo_capacity_table_v1.xlsx

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Tri-region capacity ask + SOW checklist

Laura / Marissa — forwarding Seth's note and Olga's proposed table. Need quick internal sign-off on three items before I send the cleaned PDF to procurement:

1) APAC fallback to US: compliance risk? If strict APAC residency required we need to price a separate APAC-only failover SLA and adjust baseline.
2) Burst pricing delta: Marissa, can you confirm the overage rate we should propose for burst capacity (+20% vs baseline or flat per-node overage)?
3) Ramp triggers: I pushed the usage thresholds into the spreadsheet; are the commit thresholds conservative enough for our capacity plan?

On timing — procurement wants DocuSign early next week. Olga, if you get a green from Laura/Marissa I can consolidate and push the DocuSign envelope Monday.

-Karthik

Quick notes after review:

- APAC fallback: we should avoid cross-border failover unless Edge Halo signs the APAC fallback addendum. Recommend we mark APAC -> US as "opt-in" fallback and include a security/compliance checkbox in the SOW.
- Burst pricing: propose a two-tier overage rate — transient bursts (<=48h) at X% above baseline; sustained overage (>48h) at Y% (Marissa will calculate exact % offline). This gives procurement predictability and caps sustained cost exposure.
- Ramp triggers: thresholds look fine but tighten the first tranche (to reduce immediate exposure). Recommend 60% usage trigger for first additional commit (not 50%).

I'll mark the SOW checklist with these changes and upload a redline for Olga to send.

-Laura

From: Seth Cole <seth.cole@edgehalo.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700

Thanks — that all sounds reasonable. A couple procurement items to close:

- Can you include a short clause about scheduled maintenance windows and expected impact (we need a 72h maximum per quarter for major kernel upgrades)?
- DocuSign: procurement still wants the SOW checklist embedded in the DocuSign packet and a separate statement of data residency. I attached a procurement checklist with their required headers.

If you can send the updated PDF and the DocuSign-ready SOW by EOD today we can route for internal legal review and target signature next week.

Seth

Attachments: procurement_checklist_edgehalo.pdf

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Seth Cole <seth.cole@edgehalo.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Jul 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Final: SOW draft + committed capacity table (EH-1523)

Seth / team — attaching the SOW draft (edgehalo_sow_draft_v1.pdf) and the final capacity table. Summary (finalized per internal feedback):

- Committed baseline (sustained): US 48 A100s (8 nodes), EU 24 A100s (4 nodes), APAC 24 A100s (4 nodes)
- Burst pools (pre-negotiated overage): US +20 A100s (transient up to 48h), EU +10 A100s, APAC +8 A100s; transient burst pricing X% above baseline, sustained overage Y% above baseline (to be inserted by finance)
- APAC fallback: opt-in only. If Edge Halo opts in, cross-border failover limited to stateless inference endpoints; customer must accept a separate addendum.
- Maintenance windows: quarterly scheduled maintenance up to 72h; we provide advanced notice and partial graceful degradation options in-region where possible.
- Ramp triggers: first additional commit at 60% sustained utilization over a 7-day window.

Next steps for us: Marissa will finalize the exact overage percentages and I will produce the DocuSign package. Seth — if procurement confirms the APAC opt-in language is acceptable I will attach the addendum as a separate DocuSign document.

Thanks everyone — I will send the envelope by Monday unless procurement needs it sooner.

Best regards,
Olga Petrov
Strategic Sales — Dedicated Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: edgehalo_sow_draft_v1.pdf, edgehalo_capacity_table_v1.xlsx
